plan.analysis: The seed only gives constant f (R=2/3). A much better construction is suggested by the exact identity: for f(x)=x^-1/2 on [0,L], f*f is constant π on [0,L], then decays, so R is about 0.889. This should dominate the Gaussian value 1/sqrt(2)=0.707. I will bet mainly on discretizing this singular endpoint profile, then on two independent ways to repair its decaying right half: a parametric right-end taper and a generic nonparametric local search.

experiments.hypothesis: For h(x)=x^-1/2 on [0,1], f*f equals π on [0,1], giving an almost flat autoconvolution over half its support and R around 0.889, far above the constant and Gaussian constructions.
experiments.change: Return a nonconstant step array of length N=200000 with midpoint values h[i]=((i+0.5)/N)^(-p). Compute f*f by FFT convolution, form L=[0,conv(h,h),0], and score with the exact sum formula. Use the remaining CPU time to scan p on a coarse grid in [0.47,0.53], then golden-section refine the best interval, and also compare N=100000 and N=200000 at the best p; return the best-scoring array at the largest N.
experiments.prediction: Score jumps to roughly 0.88-0.89, with best exponent near p=0.5; this will confirm the square-root endpoint profile as the new strong line.

experiments.hypothesis: The pure x^-1/2 profile has an unnecessary decaying tail of f*f on [1,2]; changing the right end of h can partially fill or reshape that tail while sacrificing only a small part of the π plateau.
experiments.change: Build x[i]=(i+0.5)/N with N=200000 starting from the square-root profile h[i]=x[i]^-0.5. Multiply it by a right-end factor phi(x)=1+a*(1-x)^q for all x in (0,1], so h[i]=x[i]^-0.5*phi(x[i]); keep h[i]=0 for x>1. Optimize the two parameters a in [-0.9,5.0] and q in [0.1,4.0] by random search followed by Nelder-Mead, evaluating R exactly via FFT convolution at each parameter value and using the whole remaining time. Return the best array found.
experiments.prediction: The optimized taper improves R above the untuned p=0.5 value, showing that the right half of f*f can be repaired parametrically; if it lowers R, the pure profile is locally optimal at the support edge.

experiments.hypothesis: The optimal h need not have an analytic form; a nonparametric local search initialized at the square-root profile can discover right-end or interior corrections that formula families miss.
experiments.change: Initialize an N=50000 array by midpoint sampling h[i]=x[i]^-0.5, x[i]=(i+0.5)/N. Optimize log(h) by stochastic block ascent: repeatedly choose a random contiguous block of width drawn log-uniformly from 1 to N/10, perturb its entries by a Gaussian vector with current scale sigma, recompute exact R by FFT convolution, and accept only improvements; halve sigma after repeated failures. Reserve about 0.5 s before budget_seconds and return the best array found.
experiments.prediction: Local search reaches or exceeds the best parametric square-root construction, and the surviving first/last cells will indicate whether a capped singular cap or an extended right tail is beneficial.

plan.analysis: p0006's pure x^-p family is the strongest line at 0.88220, close to the analytic x^-1/2 value 8/9=0.88889. Its remaining loss is the wide triangular autoconvolution tail on [1,2]. I bet on three ways to shrink/reshape that tail: (1) a smooth right-end taper inside the parametric family; (2) a localized nonparametric correction of p0005's right-end idea; (3) exact-gradient shape optimization in log-height space, which is more principled than p0007's failed local search. All should keep the plateau flat while reducing tail mass, and all must run to the deadline and return the best exact-R candidate.

experiments.hypothesis: p0006 only tunes the left singularity exponent p; multiplying by a right-end taper (1-c x)^q can reduce the triangular tail without destroying the flat plateau.
experiments.change: Replace _make(p,N) with h(x)=x^(-p)*(1-c*x)^q, x=(i+0.5)/N. Require c<1 and h>0. Optimize p in [0.49,0.52], c in [0,0.9], q in [0,10]: coarse grid (p 7 values, c 7, q 6), then Nelder-Mead or coordinate descent on exact _score at N=200000. Keep the best including start; continue until 85% of budget.
experiments.prediction: Score exceeds 0.8830 and the best has small positive c and q, showing a mild right taper helps.

experiments.hypothesis: p0005 showed the right end matters but used a coarse change; a low-dimensional multiplicative correction localized near x=1 can cancel the tail more precisely.
experiments.change: Start from p0005's returned heights (fallback p0006). Form h_i = h_i * exp(sum_{k=1}^5 c_k phi_k(x_i)), with triangular bumps phi_k centered at 0.72,0.79,0.86,0.93,0.99, half-width 0.07, and x=(i+0.5)/N. Optimize the 5 coefficients c_k by coordinate descent with step halving, rescoring exact R after each trial at N=200000. Use the full budget and return the best positive array.
experiments.prediction: Score exceeds 0.8840, improving on both p0005 and p0006 by explicitly flattening the tail knots.

experiments.hypothesis: A full-shape gradient ascent on exact R can find nonparametric corrections that scalar families miss; p0007's local search was too weak, but analytic gradients plus log-positivity should work.
experiments.change: Implement log-parameterization h=exp(u), N=50000 or 100000, initialized by resampling p0006's best shape. Compute L=conv(h,h) by FFT. Let coeff_j=(L_{j-1}+4L_j+L_{j+1})/3 and gA_m=2*sum_j coeff_j h_{j-m}; dB_m=2*sum(h); dC_m=2*h_{j*-m} at j*=argmax L (or use softmax for C). Then dR/du_m = h_m*(gA_m/(B*C) - A*(dB_m*C+B*dC_m)/(B*C)^2). Run Adam or gradient ascent with decreasing step until the deadline, always keeping the best exact-R h seen. Return best.
experiments.prediction: Score exceeds 0.8860 and the optimized shape shows a non-monotone right-end correction relative to x^-1/2.

plan.analysis: p0012 (0.882308) is barely ahead of p0010 (0.882301); the parametric family plus random log-block search is nearly saturated. The f*f profile is already flat over about half its knots, so remaining gains likely come from better edge/corner shaping and from a more effective local optimizer than random block moves. I bet on three directions: analytic gradient polishing of the full height array, a richer low-dimensional edge family seed, and a multiresolution search that buys many more cheap iterations before the expensive 200k refinement.

experiments.hypothesis: Random block perturbations are an inefficient local optimizer; the exact gradient of R with respect to log h can polish the shape and squeeze out the remaining local gain.
experiments.change: Keep p0012's seed/parametric search. Replace the final random log-block loop with full-batch gradient ascent in y=log(h), N=200000. Per iteration compute c=convolve(h,h) (FFT), Lp=[0,c,0], S=sum(a^2+ab+b^2)/3, T=sum(h), M=max(Lp), m=argmax. Set q_k=(4c_k+c_{k-1}+c_{k+1})/3 (zero outside), compute dS/dh_i=2*sum_k q_k h_{k-i} via FFT correlation, and dM/dh_i=2*h_{m-1-i} (zero outside). Then dR/dh=(dS/dh*M*T^2 - S*(2*T*M + T^2*dM/dh))/(M*T^2)^2 and grad=dR/dh*h. Normalize grad, backtracking line search on y (start step 0.5, halve up to 25 times) accepting only R increases, until the deadline. Return best h. Use process_time deadline with margin.
experiments.prediction: R rises by at least 1e-4 over 0.882308, to about 0.8824-0.8826, with the f*f plateau knots becoming more uniform.

experiments.hypothesis: p0012 fixes the left exponent at -0.5 and only uses 1+a(1-x)^q; a free left exponent plus an explicit right taper captures both ends better. p0010 tried a taper but was not polished by p0012's fine local search.
experiments.change: Keep p0012's seed evaluation, but expand its parametric family to h(x)=x^{-s}*(1+a*(1-x)^p)*(1-c*x)^q with s in [0.30,0.70], a in [-0.9,6], p in [0.1,6], c in [0,0.999], q in [0.05,5]. Add ~200 random samples plus Nelder-Mead from at least 8 seeds over these 5 parameters, scoring with the existing FFT R. Feed the best family member and p0012's original best into p0012's final local log-block search, using the remaining budget and the same deadline.
experiments.prediction: If edge mismatch is still limiting, R improves by 3e-5 to 2e-4 over 0.882308; if not, the expanded family returns essentially p0012's shape, confirming local polishing is the bottleneck.

experiments.hypothesis: p0012 spends most CPU on N=200000 FFTs and therefore takes relatively few stochastic steps; optimizing a coarse N=8000-10000 representation allows many more iterations and can find a better basin before fine refinement.
experiments.change: Start from p0012's returned array, evaluate it at N=200000, then resample it to N1=8000 by linear interpolation. Run p0012's log-space block search at N1 for about 40% of the budget, with sigma starting at 0.1, max_fails=50, and re-annealing when sigma<1e-5. Upsample the best coarse h linearly to N=200000, evaluate R, then run the same log-block search at N=200000 for the remaining budget. Always keep the best N=200000 candidate and stop near the deadline.
experiments.prediction: The coarse phase explores much more of shape space and the final R exceeds 0.882308, likely by 5e-5 to 2e-4; failure would show the 200k local search is already iteration-saturated.
